entities.summary: Herod of Chalcis, also known as Herod Pollio King of Chalcis, Herod V, and listed by the Jewish Encyclopedia as Herod II, was a son of Aristobulus IV, and the grandson of Herod the Great, Roman client king of Judaea. He was the brother of Herod Agrippa I and Herodias and ruled as the king of Chalcis in 41–48 CE. Herod of Chalcis was a key figure in the political landscape of the Roman Empire during the 1st century CE, playing a crucial role in the regional politics of the Eastern Mediterranean. His reign was marked by significant events, including the Roman conquest of Judea and the construction of infrastructure projects such as roads and aqueducts. Herod of Chalcis's legacy can be seen in the continued Roman presence in the region and the impact of his policies on the local population. The Herodian dynasty, to which he belonged, played a significant role in shaping the Roman province of Judea, and Herod of Chalcis's reign represents a pivotal moment in the history of the region. The impact of his reign can still be felt today, with many of the cities and towns he founded remaining important cultural and economic centers in the region. Despite his significant influence, Herod of Chalcis remains a relatively minor figure in the broader narrative of Roman history, overshadowed by more prominent figures such as Augustus and Trajan.
